feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 2 (lead y = 0.07 m) scored 60.41, the best so far. Iteration 3 (lead 0.08 m) scored 60.33, so lead has saturated. The s-bend progress stayed at 0.160 across leads 0.05, 0.07 and 0.08 m (iterations 1-3), and at 0.160 with the drivetrain change too. The s-bend is therefore not limited by sensing lead or by track and mass. Slalom progress has stayed at about 0.110 throughout. The oval was the only track that improved with lead. Iteration 1 showed drivetrain changes move the score by only 0.14. Every run ends off track at max_error 0.061-0.070 m with one line-loss event. This candidate tests sensor span, which is the one sensing lever left, and the weights are scaled to keep the signal gain unchanged. Depending on the next race: if the oval gains again (progress above 0.168 or max_error below 0.063) and slalom steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.16 (iteration 2 slalom was 0.149), keep the 20 mm span. If slalom oscillation rises above about 0.17 while the oval improves, the coarse spacing is making the signal non-linear near centre, so try a spacing between 15 and 20 mm (for example 17 mm, x = +/-0.034 and +/-0.017 m) before any other change. If progress on the s-bend stays at 0.160 with line_loss_events still at 1, sensing is no longer binding, and the next lever is wheel_radius for ground speed.
requested_changes: If the 20 mm span improves the oval but slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.17 (iteration 2 slalom was 0.149), try sensor spacing of 17 mm: x = +/-0.034 and +/-0.017 m at y = 0.07 m, with weights scaled to 40 times x, citing the iteration 2 slalom data.

If the s-bend still ends at progress 0.160 with max_error near 0.06 m after the span change (iterations 1-3 all gave 0.160 at different leads), try wheel_radius 0.035 m for more ground speed per wheel rotation, citing iteration 3 where lead changes did not move the s-bend.

If line_loss_events rise above 1 on any track with the 20 mm span, try sensor_size 0.016 m at the 20 mm spacing so each footprint still covers the 25 mm tape at the edge offsets, citing the iteration 2 telemetry where max_error reached 0.063 m without extra line loss.
